environment.provider_route: bounded unavailable provider at loopback port 9
environment.provider_claim: The bounded provider failure was intentional. No successful model-authored workflow claim is made.

checks.evidence: One-time pairing produced one deterministic client with exactly session:read, session:write, and credential:write. The public platform response exposed metadata only, and plaintext scans found no bearer.
Application, build, assignment, and session lookups returned one stable binding. A second nonterminal assignment for the same application returned HTTP 409.
Both applications remained revision 0 with an unchanged empty draft content hash before and after platform/daemon restarts and unavailability.

Cancellation persisted 11 contiguous daemon events and strictly acknowledged cursor 11. The terminal tail included session.status_changed, a bound assignment.cancelled event, and turn.finished; bridge relay and ack remained 11/11 after both restarts.
Last-Event-ID 8 replayed exactly sequences 9, 10, and 11, each marked replayed.
A fresh platform process using the same private data directory preserved connection/client identity, all four IDs, relay/ack cursor, and the empty draft hash.

One stop/refresh path returned explicit HTTP 503 and persisted unavailable. In a second path the connected daemon was stopped immediately before Build: HTTP 503 carried application/build/assignment/session/connection IDs with phase=recorded, storage projected unavailable, and the draft stayed empty revision 0. After daemon restart, resume retained every ID; cancellation then drained and acknowledged cursor 11/11.
Daemon restart restored the same fingerprint; refresh reconnected, and explicit rotation retained the same connection_id and client_id.
token, ToKeN, api_token, access_token, and frontend_token query variants all returned HTTP 400.
Both assignments and workflow builds remained cancelled, and the platform and daemon credentials for both assignments were durably revoked.
A 32-file scan found no platform API token, pairing code, bearer, envelope key, assignment task token, or generated pairing-code shape. Platform and daemon databases were mode 0600.

claim_ceiling: This proves the current real independent platform-to-daemon HTTP transport, private exact-scope pairing, durable four-ID binding, terminal relay/ack, replay, either-process restart, explicit unavailability, reconnect, cancellation/revocation, and no-prebuild behavior. It does not prove a successful model-authored workflow or user-operated browser path.
